article_promise: show why cross-border e-commerce can keep growing while company profit paths diverge, using four company mechanisms and explicit reversal conditions instead of a sector checklist
author_stance: the 2026 change is not a simple sector boom/bust or one-way beneficiary theme; it is a repricing of unit economics that rewards different capabilities only when financial conversion is observable
central_question: when low-value parcel institutional privilege retreats, which business capabilities can absorb or pass through customs, compliance and fulfillment costs, and how does that show up in A-share company economics?
ending_payoff: Replace the question 'which cross-border concept benefits?' with four tests: can the company remove low-quality volume, embed cost in product value, migrate the transaction model, or convert localization demand into profit—and what evidence would reverse that judgment?

opening.why_reader_should_care: The answer determines whether a company is merely exposed to cross-border e-commerce or actually has the economics to survive the new cost stack.
